title: Maximum Frequency After Subarray Operation
summary: Given an array nums of length n and an integer k, select a subarray and add an integer x to all its elements.
statement: Given an array nums of length n and an integer k, select a subarray and add an integer x to all its elements. Determine the highest frequency of the value k that can be achieved after performing this operation once.
constraints: nums has 1–100,000 values in 1..50 and k is in the same range.
Choose one nonempty subarray and add one integer x to every element in it.
Return the largest achievable frequency of k.
hints: For a chosen source value v, changing v to k gains one at v positions but loses one at existing k positions inside the same subarray.
Run maximum-subarray gain independently for each distinct source value.
Map v to +1, k to -1, and others to zero; use Kadane’s algorithm and add the best gain to the original k count.
Any useful x selects exactly one source value k-x, so enumerating those values covers every operation.
editorial: Any useful x selects exactly one source value k-x, so enumerating those values covers every operation.

tests.explanation: Changing a subarray containing the six to one adds one occurrence without losing the existing one, so the maximum is two.
Changing the subarray after the first element by eight converts its three twos to tens, yielding four tens.
